item.title: Lions Launch Christmas Card Delivery Service
item.description: The Market Harborough Twenty Twelve Lions Club has launched its fundraising Christmas Card Delivery service. For a minimum donation of 35p per card, volunteers will deliver them across the town and the Bowdens. There are postboxes at various locations, including all town centre supermarkets. item.title: Festive Road-Safety Campaign Targets Drink & Drug Drivers
item.description: Police have launched a campaign to cut the number of people killed or seriously injured by drink and drug drivers over the festive period. Increased patrols will take place on roads across Leicestershire and Northamptonshire, with officers reminding motorists of the consequences of driving under the influence. item.title: Body Of Missing Desborough Man Found
item.description: The body of a man who was reported missing from Desborough has been found in Kettering. Formal identification is yet to take place, however detectives believe the man to be 41-year-old Marc Hoodless. Marc was reported missing on September 22nd and following extensive enquiries and searches, was sadly found dead in woodland by a specialist […]

item.title: Go-Ahead For £14m Fire & Rescue Training Centre
item.description: Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service has been given the green light to build a new state-of-the-art training centre in Billesdon. The £14m facility will be built on a former highways depot off Gaulby Road and feature advanced operational zones, a multi-story fire behaviour unit, and a mock motorway section. item.title: EMR’s New Trains Enter Service
item.description: The first of East Midlands Railway’s new state-of-the-art trains has entered service today. The £400 million Aurora fleet can run on both diesel and electric power and will use the recently installed overhead wires through Market Harborough, following electrification work between Kettering and Wigston. item.title: Approval For Second Phase Of Symington Building Restoration
item.description: Work on the next phase of major renovations at Market Harborough’s historic Symington Building has been approved. The project, which will follow on-going work to repair the roof, masonry and windows at the front of the building, will cover the remainder of the site on Adam and Eve Street. item.title: Village Housing Plans Approved Despite Opposition
item.description: Plans for major housing developments in two Harborough villages have been approved, despite opposition. item.description: Harborough District Council will take no further action after a mobile phone mast it owned was removed without permission.
